propositions: The T11 migration rubric unconditionally flags post-rollback state changes, generating near-identical false-positive advisories that obscure genuine data-loss risks.

A four-condition applicability rule must replace the unconditional post-rollback paragraph to raise findings only when plans change record interpretation, rewrite records in place, remove read paths, or perform one-way transformations without back-out.

The rubric must explicitly exclude purely additive, backward-compatible persistence changes (new record/event types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults) from post-rollback-state findings.
The applicability rule must not name any store technology, ensuring portability across SQL migrations, event stores, document databases, and config formats.
